title: A comment and some resources... Hopefully!
path: RS2-1: The inanimate, physics, chemistry, astronomy

posts.content:
Hello All

I ran across Dewey Larsons RS some time ago and among others that I've found his stood out in my mind so I've been back from time to time to see 'what's new'!

I don't see how to contact the site administrator directly so I think I'm forced to post this way, sorry if this is an inappropriate way to do it! Maybe on the member page or an email address can be supplied to do this? Tks.

I wanted to mention two individuals that I think has application to RS Thory and RS2. The reason that I think they are both important is because I think that they 'have it right', at least in the areas that they address which in my opinion does cover all areas of science that can be addressed at some level. I know this is quite a statement to make so I hope that if you do visit this one site and check out this other book that there may be something of interest. Of course as usual 'Your Mileage Will Vary'!

Oh! Two sites by the same person just for 'perspective':

The person is an artist a 'Realist Painter' who has written papers on Science papers for over the last 10 years, he also has an art site where he also writes art criticism too. What he has done is address issues in such a way that I have never come across any other site on the Internet that approaches or handles problems in the mainstream such as he does. He does not propose any new theories or any exoteric math or such, he just re-runs the original papers and solves the problems in them and current issues in science too. His papers are not dense with equations but he only uses math as necessary and it's all very transparent. He also is a very good writer as well. I would suggest reading his first two papers at least and that will let you know if you want to pursue any of the other 2,000 plus pages that he has written!

http://milesmathis.com/ (main web site)

http://mileswmathis.com/ (Art Site)

http://mileswmathis.com/bio.html (Biography_

The second is a book on 'Time' also unique in all of the Internet, which I hope does not in and of it's self make it worthless!!! There is math and argument and logic here but it's not on the order of a 'theory' or of 'speculation', the author just says 'this is the way it is' and you will understand when you read the back cover 'About The Author'. I hope that this does not dissuade you from 'checking him out' so to speak! I would recommend reading the book in this order if I may... Read the entire back cover top to bottom, then read, from the very front of the book, 'Time', 'Preface', skip to the very back of the book for the 'Epilogue' and the 'Appendix'. He also writes very well with a very readable 'attitude' in his book. He does have many equations but they are necessary for his 'argument' (although he would not put it that way). The link below is to Amazons copy of it where you can browse just about the entire book before buying it. I'll put the link down for the current publisher of the book as well.

http://www.amazon.com/Time-Robert-F-Sch ... 1434991156

http://www.rosedogbookstore.com/time.html (Rosedog Books)

Article on 'Big Think' below about the book but the title is wrong however.

http://theodecorte.wordpress.com/2012/0 ... big-think/

I hope that these links will prove useful in exploring RS Theory and that of RS2 as well.

Thanks.

I don't see how to contact the site administrator directly
Under the "Navigation" menu on the right, click on "Contact." The contact form only appears when you are logged in, as there is just too much spamming for anonymous contacts.
The person is an artist a 'Realist Painter' who has written papers on Science papers for over the last 10 years,
Miles Mathis is discussed in detail in several of the forum topics on this site. Gopi has been talking with him about the RS, here: http://forum.rs2theory.org/node/409

I have not read Robert Schuyler before; will take a look. But the idea of 3D time and atoms being magnetic rotations has been around for over a half century now. Larson first discussed it in his 1959 book, Structure of the Physical Universe.
